stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
passage: In 1927, the entomologist Miriam Rothschild began cataloging the flea specimens her father, Charles Rothschild, had amassed over decades of fieldwork. The collection, numbering roughly 260,000 individual specimens representing over 900 species, was the largest of its kind in the world. Miriam Rothschild spent nearly thirty years organizing and describing the collection before donating it to the Natural History Museum in London. Her meticulous work on fleas earned her recognition as one of the foremost parasitologists of the twentieth century, despite the fact that she held no formal university degree.

options.text: Miriam Rothschild's sustained effort to document an enormous flea collection established her as a leading figure in parasitology.
Charles Rothschild's decades of fieldwork produced a flea collection that was unmatched in size by any other private or institutional holding.
The Natural History Museum in London acquired a significant entomological collection through a donation in the mid-twentieth century.
Researchers who lack formal university degrees have historically been excluded from recognition in the biological sciences.

explanation: The passage centers on Miriam Rothschild's decades-long project of cataloging her father's flea collection and the professional recognition she gained from it, making the option about her sustained documentation work and resulting reputation the best statement of the main idea. The option focusing on Charles Rothschild's fieldwork misidentifies the subject of the passage; while his collection is mentioned, the text is about Miriam's work on it, not about how he assembled it. The option about the Natural History Museum's acquisition captures only a secondary detail (the donation) rather than the passage's central point. The option claiming that researchers without degrees have been excluded contradicts the passage, which states Rothschild earned recognition despite lacking a degree, not that she was excluded.

stem: Which choice best describes the main idea of the text?
passage: Geochemist Clara Devereaux has proposed that the high concentrations of iridium found in certain deep-ocean sediment layers do not necessarily indicate asteroid impacts, as has long been assumed. Devereaux notes that volcanic eruptions from deep-mantle plumes can also deliver iridium to the Earth's surface in significant quantities. She points to the Deccan Traps, a massive volcanic province in present-day India, which was actively erupting around the same time as the Chicxulub asteroid impact 66 million years ago. Devereaux argues that distinguishing between volcanic and extraterrestrial iridium sources requires analyzing the ratios of iridium to other platinum-group elements, since mantle-derived and meteoritic materials exhibit distinct elemental signatures.

options.text: The Deccan Traps eruptions, not the Chicxulub impact, were the primary cause of the mass extinction event 66 million years ago.
Devereaux has developed a method for identifying whether iridium in sediment layers originated from volcanic activity or from asteroid impacts.
Devereaux challenges the automatic association of iridium anomalies with asteroid impacts and proposes a geochemical method to differentiate sources.
Iridium concentrations in ocean sediments are unreliable indicators of any geological event because multiple processes can deposit the element.

explanation: The passage presents two linked ideas: Devereaux's challenge to the default assumption that iridium signals asteroid impacts, and her proposal that platinum-group element ratios can distinguish volcanic from extraterrestrial sources. The option combining both elements captures the full main idea. The option about the Deccan Traps causing the mass extinction goes beyond anything Devereaux claims in the passage; she discusses iridium sourcing, not the cause of the extinction itself. The option describing a method alone captures only the second half of Devereaux's argument without the critical challenge to existing assumptions. The option calling iridium concentrations unreliable overstates the argument; Devereaux does not say iridium is unreliable, only that its source must be determined more carefully.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the text as a whole?
passage: The fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has served as a model organism in genetics for over a century, but behavioral ecologist Priya Sundaram contends that this reliance has introduced systematic blind spots. Because Drosophila thrives in laboratory conditions and reproduces rapidly, researchers have favored it for studies of gene expression, circadian rhythms, and neural development. Sundaram argues, however, that Drosophila's unusual tolerance for inbreeding and its compressed life cycle make it a poor proxy for understanding how genetic variation operates in longer-lived, outbreeding species. She does not advocate abandoning Drosophila research but instead proposes that findings from Drosophila studies be systematically cross-validated against data from organisms such as the zebrafish and the deer mouse, which more closely mirror the population structures of most vertebrates.

options.text: It presents a researcher's critique of an established scientific practice and describes the modification she recommends.
It traces the historical development of Drosophila research and explains why the organism was originally selected as a model.
It contrasts two researchers' opposing views on whether Drosophila studies should continue to receive funding.
It argues that zebrafish and deer mice should replace Drosophila as the primary model organisms in genetics research.

explanation: The passage introduces Sundaram's critique of over-reliance on Drosophila and then presents her recommended adjustment — cross-validating Drosophila findings against other organisms. The option describing a critique plus a recommended modification captures both elements. The option about tracing historical development addresses only the background information in the first sentence and misses the argumentative core. The option about two researchers' opposing views is inaccurate because only one researcher, Sundaram, is presented; no opposing figure appears. The option claiming zebrafish and deer mice should replace Drosophila overstates Sundaram's position, since she explicitly does not advocate abandoning Drosophila research but rather supplementing it with cross-validation.

stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' hypothesis?
passage: Marine biologists at the Farallon Institute have hypothesized that the recent decline in Cassin's auklet populations along the northern California coast is driven primarily by a reduction in the availability of krill, the small crustacean that constitutes the auklets' principal food source. The researchers note that ocean temperatures in the region have risen by 1.4 degrees Celsius over the past two decades, and they suspect that warmer waters have pushed krill populations deeper or farther north, beyond the auklets' typical foraging range.

options.text: Cassin's auklet colonies in Alaska, where krill remains abundant near the surface, have maintained stable population numbers over the same period.
Ocean temperatures along the northern California coast have fluctuated in similar patterns during previous decades without affecting auklet populations.
Several other seabird species that do not depend on krill have also declined in the same coastal region.
Cassin's auklets have been observed nesting in new locations farther south along the California coast in recent years.

explanation: The researchers hypothesize that reduced krill availability is driving auklet decline. The finding that auklet colonies remain stable where krill is still abundant directly supports this causal link: where the proposed cause is absent, the effect is also absent. The finding about past temperature fluctuations not affecting populations would undermine, not support, the hypothesis by suggesting temperature changes alone do not predict auklet decline. The finding about other non-krill-dependent seabirds declining would suggest a cause unrelated to krill, weakening the specific hypothesis. The finding about auklets nesting farther south does not address krill availability or population decline and could be consistent with many different explanations.

stem: Which choice best describes data from the study that would support Okonkwo's claim?
passage: Sociologist Adaeze Okonkwo has argued that multilingual households in urban Nigeria experience lower rates of intergenerational language loss than sociolinguistic models would predict. Most models assume that when a dominant language — in this case, English — pervades education, media, and commerce, heritage languages recede within two to three generations. Okonkwo contends that in cities such as Lagos and Port Harcourt, the social prestige associated with ethnic identity creates a countervailing force that sustains heritage language use even among younger, highly educated residents. To test this claim, Okonkwo surveyed 1,370 households across four Nigerian cities, tracking language use patterns among three generations within each household.

options.text: Data showing that third-generation residents in multilingual Lagos households report using their heritage language daily at rates significantly above the threshold predicted by standard language-shift models.
Data showing that English proficiency among first-generation immigrants to Lagos has increased substantially compared to earlier decades.
Data showing that heritage language instruction is offered in most public schools across the four surveyed cities.
Data showing that households in rural Nigerian communities maintain heritage languages at higher rates than urban households do.

explanation: Okonkwo claims that urban multilingual households retain heritage languages at higher rates than standard models predict. Data showing third-generation urban residents using heritage languages above model-predicted thresholds would directly confirm this claim. Data about rising English proficiency among first-generation immigrants addresses a different phenomenon — acquisition of the dominant language — and says nothing about heritage language retention across generations. Data about school-based heritage language instruction identifies a possible mechanism but does not demonstrate the outcome Okonkwo claims (lower-than-predicted language loss in households). Data about rural communities maintaining higher rates than urban ones would actually undercut Okonkwo's specific argument about urban resilience.

stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly undermine the hypothesis advanced in the text?
passage: Paleobotanist Luís Ferreira has proposed that the high density of fossilized angiosperm pollen found in Late Cretaceous sediments from the Antarctic Peninsula indicates that the region supported a diverse temperate rainforest during that period. Ferreira argues that the pollen assemblages — which include taxa closely related to modern southern beeches, tree ferns, and flowering shrubs — could only have been produced by plants growing locally, since the large, ornamented pollen grains of these species are too heavy for long-distance atmospheric transport. He further notes that the sediment layers contain leaf impressions and root traces consistent with in situ forest growth.

options.text: Experiments demonstrate that pollen grains of the size and ornamentation found in the Antarctic sediments can be carried over 3,000 kilometers by sustained polar wind currents before settling.
Fossilized pollen from coniferous species, which are associated with cooler climates, is also present in the same Antarctic sediment layers.
Late Cretaceous ocean temperatures near the Antarctic Peninsula were warmer than those observed in the region today.
Modern southern beech species produce pollen grains that are morphologically similar to those found in the Antarctic fossil record.

explanation: Ferreira's hypothesis rests on two supports: the pollen assemblages and the claim that the heavy, ornamented pollen could not have traveled long distances. A finding that such pollen can in fact be carried thousands of kilometers by polar winds directly attacks this key premise, undermining the conclusion that the plants must have grown locally. The presence of coniferous pollen in the same layers does not undermine the hypothesis; temperate rainforests can include conifers alongside angiosperms, so this finding is compatible with Ferreira's claim. Warmer ocean temperatures near the Antarctic Peninsula would, if anything, make a temperate rainforest more plausible, not less. The morphological similarity between modern southern beech pollen and the fossils supports Ferreira's taxonomic identification rather than undermining his broader claim about local growth.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: The fruit of the New Zealand tree Corynocarpus laevigatus, commonly known as karaka, contains a toxic alkaloid called karakin in its seed. Historically, Māori communities developed an elaborate multi-day process of roasting and soaking the seeds to neutralize the toxin before consumption. Archaeological evidence shows that karaka trees were deliberately planted far outside their natural coastal range, appearing at inland settlement sites dating to the fourteenth century. This distribution pattern suggests that ________

options.text: Māori communities valued karaka as a food source sufficiently to cultivate it in new environments despite the labor required to make it safe for consumption.
the karakin toxin in karaka seeds became less potent when the trees were grown in inland soils rather than coastal soils.
karaka trees were primarily cultivated for their timber rather than their fruit at inland settlement sites.
the detoxification process used by Māori communities was discovered accidentally during attempts to use karaka wood for construction.

explanation: The passage establishes that karaka seeds are toxic, that Māori developed a complex detoxification process, and that karaka trees were deliberately planted at inland sites beyond their natural range. The most logical inference linking these facts is that communities considered karaka valuable enough as food to transplant it despite the effort involved. The claim about reduced toxin potency in inland soils introduces a biological mechanism not suggested anywhere in the passage. The claim about timber cultivation contradicts the passage's focus on the fruit and its preparation for eating. The claim about accidental discovery during construction invents a narrative with no basis in the information provided.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: Economist Renata Vlasic has studied pricing patterns in independent bookstores across eleven mid-sized European cities. She found that stores located within 200 meters of a university campus charged, on average, 7 percent less for new hardcover titles than stores in other commercial districts of the same city. Vlasic notes that the campus-adjacent stores did not receive larger wholesale discounts from publishers; their cost structures were essentially identical to those of other independent bookstores. However, she also found that campus-adjacent stores sold approximately 40 percent more units per month than their counterparts elsewhere. Vlasic concludes that the lower prices at campus-adjacent stores are best explained by ________

options.text: their ability to offset thinner per-unit margins with substantially higher sales volume.
undisclosed agreements with universities that subsidize a portion of the stores' operating costs.
a preference among university students for purchasing used rather than new copies of books.
reduced competition from online retailers in areas immediately surrounding university campuses.

explanation: The passage states that campus-adjacent stores charge less despite identical costs and sell 40 percent more units. The logical conclusion connecting these facts is that higher volume compensates for lower per-unit margins, making the pricing strategy viable. The claim about university subsidies introduces an explanation with no support in the passage; Vlasic's data addresses wholesale costs and sales volume, not external subsidies. The claim about used-book preferences is irrelevant because the study specifically tracks new hardcover pricing. The claim about reduced online competition near campuses introduces a factor not mentioned or implied by the data Vlasic collected.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: Neuroscientist Tomoko Ishida has investigated how the brain processes conflicting sensory signals during locomotion. In her experiments, participants walked on a treadmill while wearing a virtual-reality headset that displayed a corridor moving at a speed different from their actual walking pace. When the visual scene moved faster than the participants were walking, most participants unconsciously increased their walking speed to match the visual flow; when the scene moved slower, they decelerated. Ishida observed, however, that participants who had undergone vestibular rehabilitation for inner-ear disorders did not show this automatic speed adjustment. These participants maintained a steady walking pace regardless of the visual scene's speed. Ishida argues that this contrast suggests that ________

options.text: the automatic gait adjustment observed in most participants depends on integration between visual input and vestibular feedback, and that vestibular rehabilitation alters how the brain weights these competing signals.
participants who had undergone vestibular rehabilitation were unable to perceive the visual scene displayed by the virtual-reality headset during the experiment.
the virtual-reality display used in the experiment was not realistic enough to produce sensory conflict in participants with prior exposure to similar technology.
visual processing speed is primarily determined by vestibular function, and damage to the inner ear permanently eliminates the brain's ability to interpret visual motion.

explanation: The passage shows that most participants automatically adjusted gait to match visual flow, but vestibular-rehabilitation participants did not. The most logical inference is that automatic adjustment requires integration of visual and vestibular signals, and rehabilitation changed how the brain prioritizes these inputs. The claim that rehabilitation participants could not perceive the visual scene is unsupported and implausible; the passage describes altered motor response, not perceptual blindness. The claim about the headset lacking realism is contradicted by the fact that most participants did respond to the visual display, confirming its effectiveness at producing sensory conflict. The claim that vestibular function determines visual processing and that inner-ear damage eliminates visual motion interpretation vastly overstates the findings; the passage discusses gait adjustment in response to conflicting signals, not a wholesale loss of visual motion perception.
